questiontext.text: For an order-n magic square using 1..n2, the magic constant (each line's sum) equals...

feedback.text: Correct — total 1+...+n^2 divided by n rows.
That is the number of cells, not the line sum.
That is the sum of 1..n, not the magic constant.
Too small; this ignores the n^2 terms.

generalfeedback.text: The numbers 1..n^2 sum to n^2(n^2+1)/2; dividing among n rows gives n(n^2+1)/2 per line.

questiontext.text: In a magic square, which sets of cells all share the same sum?

answer.text: every row, every column, and both main diagonals

feedback.text: Correct — all these lines equal the magic constant.
Columns and diagonals also match.
Rows and columns match too.
Corners are not a defining line.

generalfeedback.text: Rows, columns, and the two main diagonals all sum to n(n^2+1)/2.

questiontext.text: In the Siamese (De la Loubere) method for odd order, where is the number 1 placed?

feedback.text: Correct — the middle column of the top row.
The Siamese method starts at the top-middle, not the corner.
The center holds the middle value, not 1.
That is not the standard starting cell.

generalfeedback.text: Place 1 at the top-middle, then repeatedly move up-and-right.

questiontext.text: In the Siamese method, when the up-and-right cell is already filled, you instead...

answer.text: drop down one cell from the current cell

feedback.text: Correct — when blocked, move down one instead.

answer.text: move two cells to the right

feedback.text: The rule is to drop down one, not skip right.
You do not restart; you drop down one cell.
The construction continues after dropping down.

generalfeedback.text: Default move is up-and-right (wrapping); if that cell is taken, place the next number directly below the current one.

questiontext.text: Both main diagonals of a magic square sum to the magic constant.

feedback.text: Correct — the two main diagonals also equal the constant.
Both main diagonals do sum to the magic constant.

questiontext.text: The Siamese method starts by placing 1 in the top-left corner cell.

feedback.text: It starts at the top-middle cell, not the top-left corner.
Correct — 1 goes in the top-middle cell.

questiontext.text: The shared sum of every row, column, and diagonal, equal to n(n^2+1)/2, is called the magic ______.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Accepted — the diagonals also sum to this constant.

questiontext.text: Which statements about odd-order magic squares (Siamese method) are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: Every row, column, and main diagonal sums to n(n^2+1)/2

feedback.text: Yes — that is the magic constant.

answer.text: Construction starts at the top-middle cell moving up-and-right

feedback.text: Yes — the Siamese default move.

answer.text: When blocked, you move two cells to the right

feedback.text: No — you drop down one cell.

answer.text: Only the rows need to sum to the constant

feedback.text: No — columns and both diagonals must too.

generalfeedback.text: All lines sum to n(n^2+1)/2; start top-middle, move up-right, and drop down one when blocked.
